title: Seven Hills and a River
objective: After this level you can explain how the Tiber and the seven hills shaped where and why Rome grew.
summary: Rome grew at a crossing of the Tiber on a trade route, on hills that were easy to defend and stayed dry. Ostia became its port.

cards.headline: Why build a city right here? Follow the river and the salt.
cards.body: Rome sits where it does for reasons you can still see on a map: a river you can cross, a road for salt, and hills that keep your feet dry.

cards.headline: A river crossing
cards.body: Rome grew where the Tiber River could be crossed, near an island in the river, about 25 km from the sea. An ancient salt route, later called the Via Salaria, passed right through, linking the coast with inland Italy. So anyone moving goods between the two came this way. Own the crossing, and trade has to walk past your front door.
cards.callout: River crossing + trade route = a place worth holding

cards.headline: Seven hills
cards.body: The city spread across seven hills beside the Tiber, among them the Capitoline and the Palatine, where those first huts stood. The hills made sense twice over. They were easier to defend, and they stayed dry when the Tiber flooded the low ground between them. Enemies and floods: the hills handled both.

cards.context: Rome sat about 25 km inland, so its harbor was downstream. Ostia, at the mouth of the Tiber, became Rome’s port. Grain and other goods came in there and traveled up the river to the city. The same river that gave Rome its crossing also delivered dinner.

cards.headline: Rome’s geography: mapped
learned: Rome grew at a crossing of the Tiber
A salt route passed through its site
Seven hills gave defense and dry ground

questions.prompt: Beside which river was Rome built?

options.label: The Po
options.rationale: The Po runs across northern Italy.

questions.explanation: Rome grew beside the Tiber, at a point where the river could be crossed.

questions.prompt: Why did early Romans prefer to live on the hills?

options.label: They were closer to the sea
options.rationale: The coast is about 25 km away.

options.label: They were easier to defend and stayed dry
The soil there was best for vines

questions.explanation: Hills could be defended, and they stayed above the Tiber’s floods.

questions.prompt: From Level 3: on which of the seven hills are Rome’s earliest known huts?

options.label: The Janiculum
options.rationale: It isn’t one of the traditional seven.

questions.explanation: Iron Age hut remains have been found on the Palatine, one of the seven hills.
